headline: Bruins crush Predators while Patriots endure a heartbreaker in Chicago
morning_brew: Thursday night was a straight-up Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde experience for Boston sports fans. The Bruins absolutely dismantled the Predators at the Garden, looking like the kind of juggernaut that makes me wanna start looking at flight prices for the Cup Final. Putting up six goals against an NHL opponent is a thing of beauty, and seeing the scoring spread out across the lineup feels like a major deposit into the Duck Boat fund. It was a clean, clinical demolition that wiped the taste of that earlier overtime slip-up right out of my mouth, and frankly, I could get used to nights where I don't have to watch through my fingers like I'm sitting through a horror movie.

On the flip side, the football result out in Chicago was a kick in the teeth that still stings this morning. We hung in there, but we just didn't have the juice to close out the Bears when it mattered most, and that is a special kind of misery. It is agonizing to watch us go toe-to-toe and come up short because of a few plays. Drake Maye showed some serious flashes of brilliance, but my neighbor Rick is currently six hours into a conspiracy theory about the play-calling that would make a tinfoil hat look reasonable, and as much as I want to tell him to take a hike, I am feeling every bit of that gloom right along with him.

We have to shake it off, because the calendar never stops for a pity party. The C's are back at the Garden tonight to square up with the Knicks, and I am itching to see them erase the memory of that opener. It is a massive early test to see if they can handle their business on their own parquet. I will be glued to the tube again, praying for a win because I'm not sure how much more of this cardiac-event sports schedule my ticker can take. Let's see if the boys can channel some of that Bruins energy and get us back on the right side of the ledger.

trend_watch.dans_take: When Pasta is playing like he's skating on a frozen pond in his backyard, there isn't a goalie on earth who can stop him.

trend_watch.trend: Finished the night with two passing touchdowns and a rushing score against Chicago.
trend_watch.dans_take: The kid has the heart of a lion, but watching him carry the whole building on his back is gonna give me gray hair.

trend_watch.trend: Stopped all twenty-eight shots he faced to earn the win.
trend_watch.dans_take: A perfect night in the crease is exactly what the doctor ordered to keep my blood pressure from hitting triple digits.
